Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Krishna identifies this destructive force as insatiable desire or lust (kama), born from the mode of passion. When frustrated, it transforms into anger (krodha), serving as the primary internal enemy of self-mastery.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Identifying the ultimate root cause of compulsive behavior and emotional volatility.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna names the enemy: it is desire (kama) born of rajo-guna, which transforms into anger (krodha) when blocked. He characterizes it as all-devouring and the worst internal adversary.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is given clear clarity on the exact psychological root of self-destructive behavior.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Uncontrolled Desire: Insatiable cravings that distort healthy decision-making
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Frustration-Aggression Escalation: The rapid shift from blocked desire to intense anger
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Identifying Internal Adversaries: Pinpointing specific internal triggers behind psychological distress

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kama esa krodha esa rajo-guna-samudbhavah (Lust and anger originating from the mode of passion)
Mahasano maha-papma viddhy enam iha vairinam (Know this insatiable, all-devouring force as the enemy here)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna identifies unbridled desire (kama), born of the mode of passion, as the primary enemy. When blocked, it turns into destructive anger (krodha), dragging the soul down into material entanglement.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Unchecked craving distorts reality, and when blocked, predictably manifests as anger and resentment. Identifying craving as the root cause allows you to manage impulses before they escalate into emotional outbursts.
